items.title: Brier Score Tracking
items.action: get_brier_score()/get_market_baseline_brier_score() already existed but only ever computed a single CURRENT-MOMENT aggregate over all resolved signals at call time -- nothing persisted a point-in-time value, so there was no way to see whether calibration is improving or degrading run over run. log_run() now snapshots both scores (plus the n they were computed over) onto each run row via 3 new columns on the runs table (brier_scorer, brier_market, brier_n) -- required generalizing _add_col() (previously hardcoded to ALTER TABLE signals) to take a table= parameter so it could migrate runs too. brier_n is NULL, not 0, for any run logged before this existed or where 0 signals had resolved yet at that point -- distinguishes "not measured" from "measured zero." Added get_brier_history() to read the series back oldest-first for a future trend view. Found and fixed a bug introduced while writing the new tests: an Edit meant to append a trailing assertion onto test_log_run_idempotent_replace instead displaced it into the newly-added test_get_brier_history_ordered_oldest_first (which has no `rows` variable in scope), raising a NameError -- caught by running the targeted test slice before committing, moved back to the correct test. Also had to extend the migration test's stub old-schema `signals` table with timestamp/ticker columns, since _init_db()'s CREATE INDEX statements reference them unconditionally. 13 new tests (schema, migration-preserves-existing-rows, log_run snapshot storage, get_brier_history empty/NULL-exclusion/ordering). Full suite: 2103 passed, 0 failed.
items.notes: 25 resolved signals gives a stable enough baseline to detect systematic miscalibration.

items.title: Confluence Detection
items.action: main.py already computed _count_agreeing_signals() (Polymarket price gap, cross-market consensus, whale detection, orderbook imbalance, watchlist alignment) but only persisted it as ext_n_signals when the extremizing transform's own alpha>1.0 threshold fired -- n=0 and n=1 were both NULL in the DB, indistinguishable from each other and from "not computed yet." Added confluence_count, recorded unconditionally on every YES/NO signal regardless of whether extremizing itself fires. Added get_stats_by_confluence() (win rate/PnL/avg edge/Brier bucketed by 0/1/2+ agreeing sources, same bucketing convention as get_stats_by_watchlist()) and a matching "BY CONFLUENCE" section in analysis/calibration.py's report, plus confluence_count added to the CSV export whitelist. While wiring the new column into both signals-table INSERT paths, found and fixed a real latent bug in log_pass(): its VALUES clause has a differently-laid-out placeholder count than log_signal()'s (wraps across two lines), so the shared column-list edit updated the Python binding tuple but not the SQL placeholder count, causing every log_pass() call to fail silently with "Incorrect number of bindings supplied" until corrected -- caught via 7 collateral test failures in the full suite, none directly about confluence. 8 new tests (schema, both INSERT paths, get_stats_by_confluence bucketing/win-rate/Brier/NULL-exclusion/PASS-exclusion). No data exists yet with a resolved outcome and a non-NULL confluence_count (field just added), so get_stats_by_confluence()'s real-world verdict is unproven until enough new paper signals resolve -- calibration.py's new section explicitly reports "No resolved data yet" rather than fabricating a false 0%. Full suite: 2103 passed, 0 failed.
items.notes: Multi-source agreement historically lifts win rates and needs resolved data to measure the effect.

items.title: Edge Decay Analysis

items.title: Market-Price Baseline Brier
items.action: For every resolved signal, compute and persist the Brier score of the market price at scan time alongside the existing scorer Brier. Expose our_estimate, brier_scorer and brier_market as explicit columns in data/powerbi_export/signals.csv, and surface both Brier figures in analysis/calibration.py output.
items.notes: The scorer prompt injects current market price (core/scorer.py:649) and explicitly instructs anchoring to it (scorer.py:245-253), so scorer Brier alone cannot distinguish real edge from price echo. Arithmetic on data already in the DB, so no gate. Must exist before resolved_count clears the brier-tracking gate at 25. SHIPPED 2026-07-23: market_baseline_brier column (core/logger.py, additive migration), computed+persisted at resolution time in resolve_outcomes() and via backfill_market_baseline_brier() for the 10 pre-existing resolved rows with a usable market_price (1 of 11 has no market_price and is correctly left NULL, never coerced to 0.5). get_market_baseline_brier_score() mirrors get_brier_score() exactly. Surfaced in analysis/calibration.py (side by side with scorer Brier, plus a verdict line) and in the signals.csv export (scorer_brier computed column + persisted market_baseline_brier). Real result on the current n=8 paper population: scorer Brier 0.0578 vs baseline 0.0022 -- scorer currently WORSE than the market price, exactly the anchoring risk this metric exists to catch. See docs/PROGRESS.md 2026-07-23.

items.title: Pre-Registered Kill Criteria
items.action: Write docs/PREREGISTRATION.md stating, in advance and dated, the result at n=50 that would falsify the edge hypothesis and halt signal development. Specify the metric (scorer Brier vs market-baseline Brier), the margin required, and what happens if it is not met.
items.notes: No code. Worthless if written after the data is seen. Same discipline as the IDEAS.md append-only rule, applied to results instead of scope. Append-only once committed. SHIPPED 2026-07-25: docs/PREREGISTRATION.md written. Pre-registers a PAIRED comparison (brier_market_i - brier_scorer_i per resolved row, using the existing brier_component() and the source=paper/result-resolved/direction-valid/both-values-present population) evaluated at the first paired n>=50, with a 95% CI (z=1.96, matching core.report._wilson_ci existing convention) on the mean paired delta as the pass/fail bar -- a raw point-estimate comparison is explicitly insufficient. Defines exactly what "halt signal development" means (new heuristics/scoring changes halt; price-blind-arm, replay validation, and this document's own amendment are explicitly not halted) and requires a written post-mortem before resuming. Current state recorded for dating purposes only (paired n=8 as of writing, well below the n=50 checkpoint) -- not a checkpoint evaluation. Append-only from here.

items.title: LLM Daily Cost Ceiling
items.action: Add a configurable daily spend cap in core/llm.py that accumulates cost_usd across calls and raises once breached. Surface the running total in the daily report footer.
items.notes: Per-call cost is computed at core/llm.py:146 but nothing enforces a limit. Prerequisite for replay-runner, which will multiply scoring volume. SHIPPED 2026-07-25: daily_cost_ceiling_usd (config.json llm section, default $20/day) enforced in core/llm.py via _check_cost_ceiling(), called BEFORE issuing each API request in both score_via_api and probe_via_api so a caller looping over many markets (replay-runner) stops making new calls the moment the ceiling is hit, not just after the breaching call already ran. Running total persists in data/llm_daily_cost.json (gitignored, same pattern as gate_state.json), resets on UTC day rollover, survives process restarts, shared across every caller (research probes, eval re-scoring, future replay-runner). Only applies to real metered API spend -- the main scan (backend=cli, Pro subscription) has no per-token bill and is unaffected. Surfaced in both the text and HTML daily report footers via core.llm.get_daily_cost_usd(). See docs/PROGRESS.md 2026-07-25.

items.title: Settled Market Fetcher
items.action: Pull Kalshi settled markets with their final outcomes, reaching further back than the local snapshot archive begins. Persist to a dedicated table separate from live signals.
items.notes: Read-only against existing tables. Local snapshots only reach 2026-07-08, so the archive alone caps corpus size well below what is useful. SHIPPED 2026-07-25: core.kalshi.fetch_settled_events()/fetch_settled_event_markets() (event-based, not /markets?status=settled directly -- that endpoint is 999/1000 KXMVE parlays, confirmed empirically; the event-based path is 0/400 KXMVE) plus backtesting/settled_fetcher.py persisting to a new settled_markets table (series_ticker/category carried from the event, idempotent INSERT OR IGNORE keyed on ticker, read-only against signals/runs -- confirmed by test). Real backfill run: 1999/2000 events scanned (1 transient connection reset, caught and skipped), 12,681 markets fetched, 12,593 inserted, 81 skipped as unresolved. Table now holds 12,600 rows across 1,203 events / 656 series, close_time spanning 2026-05-19 to 2026-07-25 -- 4,505 rows (36%) predate the 2026-07-08 local snapshot floor this item exists to fix. See docs/PROGRESS.md 2026-07-25.

items.title: As-Of Market State Reconstruction
items.action: Given a ticker and a historical date, reconstruct the market state as it stood then, sourcing from data/snapshots where available and Kalshi history beyond that. Output must match the dict shape core.scorer.score_markets already consumes.
items.notes: Matching the existing input shape is the hard requirement. If reconstruction emits a different shape the scorer gets modified to accommodate it, which breaks comparability with live signals and defeats the point. SHIPPED 2026-07-25: backtesting/asof_reconstruction.py::reconstruct_market_state(config, ticker, as_of_date) -- two source tiers tried in order, EXACT (data/snapshots/*.json, point-in-time raw dump) then APPROXIMATE (core.kalshi.fetch_market_candlesticks(), new function, daily close-of-period candle), returns None (never fabricates) if neither has data for that ticker/date. Reuses core.scanner.score_market() verbatim on the reconstructed raw dict rather than reimplementing any scanner/heuristic logic, guaranteeing exact shape match with what core.scorer.score_markets() consumes; confirmed via grep that score_market() and everything it calls (compute_drift_signal, compute_whale_reversal, compute_spread_signal, estimate_base_rate, get_heuristic_label, kalshi_fee) are pure functions of the market dict + config, no datetime.now() anywhere in that path, so replaying a historical as_of_date can't leak today's wall-clock context. whale_data/poly/watchlist_signal are permanently absent on replayed markets (main.py steps 4-6 enrichments have no historical archive) -- a structural limit of replay, not a bug. CORRECTION: this item's own action text and replay-settled-fetcher's note above both assumed data/snapshots only reaches back to 2026-07-08 -- that was never actually checked against the files on disk. Directory listing on 2026-07-25 shows 92 snapshot files starting 2026-06-16, three weeks earlier; core/kalshi.py and settled_fetcher.py's docstrings have been corrected, this note is left as the historical record of the error. Separately discovered (out of scope, flagged to user, not fixed here): core.kalshi.fetch_market_history() -- the OLDER, still-live function main.py:364 calls for the price-trend feature -- hits /markets/{ticker}/history, which does not exist on Kalshi's API (confirmed empirically: every ticker tried returns a plain-text 404, never JSON); the function's `if status==404: return []` has silently swallowed this for every call site, meaning that feature has never actually returned data. Needs its own backlog item. See docs/PROGRESS.md 2026-07-25.

items.title: Retroactive Replay Runner
items.action: Drive backtesting/harness.py over the reconstructed corpus and grade each replayed score against the known settled outcome. Write results to a table physically separate from live paper signals.
items.notes: Replayed scores are contaminated by look-ahead: the model's training data and web search both know how these resolved. Separation must be enforced in schema, not by convention, so no later query can accidentally pool the two populations. SHIPPED 2026-07-25: backtesting/replay_runner.py -- run_replay(config, max_markets) samples settled_markets tickers not yet replayed, reconstructs each at the furthest-from-close lookback (30/14/7/3/1 days) whose mid_price still falls within config.markets.min_market_price/max_market_price (the live pipeline's own price band, reused rather than inventing a new threshold, to avoid trivially 'backtesting' a market already telegraphed by consensus price -- verified against real candlestick trajectories before choosing this rule), scores it via core.scorer.score_markets() with backend forced to 'api' (real metered billing + the daily cost ceiling this item depends on -- the CLI/Pro path has no cost concept and would defeat the ceiling), and persists to a new replay_signals table (idempotent INSERT OR IGNORE on ticker, never joined with live signals). export_and_report() writes a separate replay_signals.csv/replay_resolutions.csv pair and drives the existing, UNMODIFIED backtesting.harness.BacktestRunner over them. Added an additive `now` override to core.scorer.build_prompt()/score_markets() (default None -> real datetime.now(), unchanged for every live caller) so replayed prompts describe days-remaining relative to the as-of date, not today -- verified the days-left text renders correctly for a historical date. Tests: tests/test_replay_runner.py (+19, core.scorer.score_markets mocked throughout -- no real API spend in the test suite), plus a manual dry run against the REAL settled_markets/candlestick data (only the paid scoring call stubbed) that correctly found 5 of 9 candidates reconstructable and price-band-legitimate. Full suite: 1758 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. KNOWN SIMPLIFICATION: does not replicate main.py's post-hoc confidence-downgrade business rules (HIGH->MED gates) -- grades Claude's raw response as returned. LOOK-AHEAD CONTAMINATION remains a permanent, structural limitation of what replay results can mean, not something schema separation fixes -- see the module docstring. NOT YET DONE, deliberately held for explicit go-ahead: an actual real-cost batch run against the API. Every prior real-cost action this session (main.py's live run) got a heads-up first; this one forces metered billing where the live path normally has none, so the same courtesy applies before the first genuine invocation. See docs/PROGRESS.md 2026-07-25.

items.title: Instrument Validation On Replay Corpus
items.action: Using the replay corpus at n>=300, verify the measurement apparatus: grading handles early closes, voided markets and multi-outcome events; baseline Brier computes correctly across the full price range; the resolved_count >= 10 smart-money wallet threshold is empirically defensible.
items.notes:
This tests the instrument, not the forecaster. Contaminated data cannot establish edge and no edge claim may cite it. The value is discovering broken grading logic now instead of at n=25 with live signals that took three months to accumulate.

PARTIAL VERIFICATION 2026-07-26 (item stays `ready` -- this only covers the grading-edge-cases clause, not the Brier-across-price-range or resolved_count>=10 clauses, both of which need the live n>=300 corpus): checked the three named edge cases against real production data and existing tests rather than assuming. (1) Voided markets: settled_fetcher._row_from_market() already returns None for any result not in (YES, NO), confirmed by tests/test_settled_fetcher.py::test_skips_unresolved_markets_within_a_settled_event -- voided markets never enter settled_markets at all. (2) Multi-outcome events: queried the real settled_markets table (12,600 rows) -- confirmed both mutually-exclusive events (e.g. KXLIUSACOUPLE-26AUG31, 182 sibling tickers, exactly 1 YES) and legitimately non-exclusive ones (e.g. KXPGATOP10-THOC26, 156 tickers, 13 YES) exist in the real corpus. replay_runner._row_from_scored() grades strictly per-ticker with no event-level aggregation or exclusivity assumption anywhere in the code path, so both patterns are handled correctly by construction -- confirmed by tests/test_replay_runner.py's test_row_from_scored_* tests, none of which reference sibling tickers at all. (3) Early closes: hypothesized that a stale close_time (reflecting an originally -scheduled deadline rather than actual early closure) could let as-of reconstruction sample market state from AFTER real resolution, contaminating the replay with look-ahead price data. Checked this empirically against all 12,600 real settled_markets rows: settlement_ts never precedes close_time (min gap +22s, max +3.4 days, 0 negative gaps) -- close_time already reflects actual closure in every observed case, not a stale scheduled date, so this risk does not materialize in the real data. No code change made -- no bug found, and existing test coverage for (1) and (2) already locks in the correct behavior; writing new tests would have duplicated it. depends_on (replay-runner, market-baseline-brier) both already done; still blocked on the same broken Anthropic API key (401 authentication_error, re-confirmed this session) for generating the n>=300 corpus this item's remaining clauses require.

items.title: Price-Blind Scoring Arm
items.action: Add a scoring mode that omits the Current market price line and all market-anchoring instructions. Run it on a sampled subset of scored markets daily and log to a separate column. Do not feed it into signal selection.
items.notes: SHIPPED 2026-07-26: core/blind_scorer.py adds a price-blind shadow scoring mode. Not just scorer.SYSTEM_PROMPT with the price line deleted -- the live prompt leaks price-derived info in several other places (FLAG REASON compares a heuristic base rate to market price, SIGNAL QUALITY is derived from net_edge, and the HEURISTIC/POLYMARKET/CONSENSUS conflict warnings are keyed off heuristic_direction, itself computed from base_rate vs Kalshi's own mid_price) -- all of these are stripped in build_prompt_blind(), which shows only ticker/title/horizon/close-date/WHALE ALERT, not just the literal price line. SYSTEM_PROMPT_BLIND is scorer.SYSTEM_PROMPT plus an appended override block (not a hand-copied duplicate of all ~47 calibration rules, which would silently drift the moment someone edits a live rule) -- most rules are pure category base-rate guidance that never mentions price and carries over unchanged; only the handful that are STRUCTURALLY about comparing to market price (Rules 1, 11, 13, 28, 29, 30, 32, 35) get a concrete, price-free replacement instruction, not just a 'disregard this' note -- e.g. Rule 11's edge requirement is replaced with 'report a raw estimate and confidence, no direction/edge field', Rule 35's CME-FedWatch-vs-Kalshi-gap mechanic is replaced with 'report the FedWatch-implied probability directly'. Always scored via a new core.llm.score_blind_via_api() (RECORD_BLIND_SCORES_TOOL: ticker/estimate/confidence/reasoning/sources_checked -- no market_price/edge/direction fields, since there's no price to diff against), forced regardless of config.llm.backend -- the sample-rate-vs-daily-cost-ceiling constraint the item calls for is only enforceable through core.llm's metered _check_cost_ceiling gate, which score_blind_via_api shares with score_via_api/probe_via_api (same daily total, not a separate budget). Results are persisted to a new, structurally separate `blind_scores` SQLite table (core.logger.log_blind_score) -- never `signals` -- so the shadow arm is architecturally unable to feed signal selection, not just unused by convention. main.py wires this in as a non-fatal step after final_signals is already decided: main._sample_for_blind_arm() picks up to config.blind_arm.sample_size markets (default 3, deterministic first-N for reproducibility) from those the anchored scorer already scored, and any failure is caught and logged, never raised. Gated behind config.blind_arm.enabled, defaulting to false in both config.json and config.example.json -- unlike the main scan (Pro subscription, no per-token bill), every run this fires spends real metered API cost, so it needs a deliberate opt-in rather than activating silently as a side effect of this backlog item. build_prompt_blind() smoke-tested against real live Kalshi market dicts (KXCANADACUP-30, KXNFLENDSTREAK-40NYJ-3031) -- renders cleanly, no KeyErrors on real production field shapes. score_blind_via_api() itself cannot be validated end-to-end: the real Anthropic API key still returns 401 authentication_error on every live call (same blocker as replay-instrument-validation), so this is implemented and unit/mock-tested (18 tests across tests/test_blind_scorer.py, tests/test_llm.py, tests/test_blind_arm_main.py, tests/test_logger_blind_scores.py) but not yet run for real -- enable config.blind_arm.enabled once the key works and the user wants to start spending on it. Full suite green (1844 passed, 1 skipped). See docs/PROGRESS.md 2026-07-26.

items.title: Unattended Operation Hardening
items.action: Alert on absence rather than presence: notify if no successful run has completed within N hours. Add graceful degradation when an upstream API changes shape, and a runbook in docs/ for diagnosing a failed run without reloading full project context.
items.notes: SHIPPED 2026-07-26: implemented all three pieces of unattended operation hardening. (1) Absence alerting: scripts/heartbeat_check.py checks the most recent core.logger runs row and emails an alert if none exists within max_silence_hours (default 30.0), using the same fire-once JSON state-file pattern as scripts/gate_notifier.py (state only persists after a successful send, so a failed send retries next run rather than silently giving up). Registered via scripts/setup_heartbeat_scheduler.ps1 as an independent Windows Task (Leviathan-Heartbeat, 2:00 PM and 8:00 PM daily) rather than chained after the main run, since its entire purpose is detecting that the main run's own scheduler stopped firing. Smoke-tested against the real DB (python scripts/heartbeat_check.py --dry-run -> 'OK -- last run 8.9h ago'). 11 tests in tests/test_heartbeat_check.py, all passing. (2) Graceful degradation on API shape change: main.py gained _validate_market_shape(), checking every fetched market for ticker/close_time/yes_bid_dollars/yes_ask_dollars/title (the fields filter_markets/score_market assume exist). Wired into step 2 right after the existing fetch/fallback try/except: if >=config.markets.shape_anomaly_min_sample (default 20) markets were fetched and more than shape_anomaly_threshold (default 50%) of them are missing at least one required field, the run aborts before scoring and sends an ALERT email via the existing send_report() rather than silently processing what's likely a Kalshi response-shape change as if it were real, complete data. Both thresholds added to config.json/config.example.json. 6 tests in tests/test_market_shape_validation.py, all passing. (3) docs/RUNBOOK.md added, covering the three failure modes an absence alert can't distinguish on its own (scheduler didn't fire / task fired but the run failed early, most commonly Kalshi auth / crashed uncaught mid-pipeline), the empty-runs-table case, and the shape-anomaly-abort case -- the latter explicitly cross-references the 2026-07-25 fetch_orderbook/fetch_trades bug sweep as precedent for how a genuine Kalshi shape change gets diagnosed and fixed. Full suite green after all three pieces (1823 passed, 1 skipped). See docs/PROGRESS.md 2026-07-26.

items.title: Multi-Sample Score Aggregation
items.action: score_markets() (core/scorer.py) took config["scoring"]["multi_sample_n"] (default 1, unchanged behavior) -- when set >1, runs the SAME batch/prompt through the configured backend that many times independently and merges results via the new _aggregate_multi_sample(), instead of trusting a single pass. RESPONSE_SCHEMA defines direction as DERIVED per-pass from comparing that pass's own our_estimate to market_price ("YES if our_estimate > market_price and edge is worth acting on"), so a 0.7-YES sample and a 0.5-PASS sample are answers to two different implicit questions -- averaging our_estimate across disagreeing directions would blend framings. Design: direction is decided by majority vote across the N per-ticker samples; a genuine tie (e.g. 2 YES/2 NO, or an even split with no literal PASS votes at all) breaks to PASS as the conservative default rather than coin-flipping a side -- this tie-break rule was a judgment call made without asking the user first, since it's easily reversible code, not a data/business decision. our_estimate is then the mean taken ONLY over the samples that agreed with the winning direction (a fallback to averaging over every sample handles the edge case where PASS wins via tie-break but zero samples literally said PASS, avoiding a divide-by-zero on an empty agreeing-pool). edge is recomputed fresh from that aggregate estimate vs market_price rather than trusting any single sample's self-reported edge. confidence/reasoning are taken from whichever agreeing sample's own our_estimate is closest to the aggregate mean (the most "representative" individual call) -- there's no principled way to average a HIGH/MED/LOW enum or a reasoning string. sources and sources_checked are unioned (deduped by url / by string) across every agreeing sample, since each pass is a genuinely independent research pass. A ticker missing from some passes (a parse hiccup, or Claude omitting it from one pass's JSON array) is aggregated over however many passes did include it, with n_samples on the result recording how many of the N actually agreed. rescore_single_market() (a separate, already-existing single-market path built for per-pick source attribution when publishing subscriber picks -- see GOAL_phase2-6_decisions.md Decision 1) was deliberately left untouched: the backlog item text named score_markets specifically, and rescore_single_market solves a structurally different problem this change doesn't touch. multi_sample_n added to config.example.json documented at its default (1, off) -- the live config.json was deliberately NOT changed to enable multi-sampling by default, since turning it on multiplies the CLI backend's (the default, config.llm.backend="cli") scoring-step wall-clock time by roughly Nx per scheduled run; the CLI backend has no per-token dollar cost (rides the Pro OAuth subscription, not metered billing), but the runtime and Pro-plan-usage multiplication is real and hadn't been weighed against any specific N before this session. 22 new tests in tests/test_scorer.py (12 on _aggregate_multi_sample directly: unanimous/majority/tie-to-PASS/PASS-majority/edge-recompute/representative-confidence-reasoning/sources-union/sources_checked-union/partial-ticker-coverage/_validate_scores compatibility; 4 on score_markets' multi_sample_n wiring: default-is-single-call, N-calls-backend-N-times for both CLI and API backends, N=1-explicit-matches-default, API token_info summed correctly across passes). Full suite: 2117 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed.
items.notes: Single-pass scoring absorbs full LLM sampling variance into signal selection. Gated because it shifts the estimate distribution and makes pre-change and post-change resolutions non-comparable.

items.title: Power BI Export Schema Hardening
items.action: Add run_id to data/powerbi_export/signals.csv as a foreign key to runs.csv. Confirm the source column reliably distinguishes live paper signals from any future replay corpus rows. Audit every column where blank currently appears and document, per column, whether blank means not-computed or zero.
items.notes: signals.csv and runs.csv share no join key today, so Power BI cannot relate signals to the cost, token and runtime data in runs.csv, and joining on date is ambiguous because the pipeline runs twice daily. The source discriminator must exist and be filtered on before replay-runner produces look-ahead-contaminated rows; adding it while it has a single value is free, retrofitting it later means auditing every visual for silent contamination. Blank vs zero matters because Power BI AVERAGE skips blanks: net_edge and base_rate are blank on 37 of 182 rows, close_time on 25. SHIPPED 2026-07-24: run_id added as an explicit FK column in signals.csv (165/182 rows populated -- every paper row has one; the 17 blank rows are real_fill/research_probe, which structurally never get a run_id, confirmed via backfill_run_id() finding 0 backfillable + 17 genuinely unrecoverable, never guessed via nearest-timestamp matching). source discriminator confirmed populated on all 182 rows, but the notes assumption was WRONG -- 3 distinct values exist today (paper/real_fill/research_probe), not just paper; the paper-only filter already used throughout core/logger.py correctly excludes the other two regardless. Full blank-vs-zero audit written to docs/POWERBI_EXPORT_SCHEMA.md -- every blank column means not-computed, never zero; no existing values altered. See docs/PROGRESS.md 2026-07-24.

items.title: Fix Broken Live Price-History Endpoint
items.action: core.kalshi.fetch_market_history() calls /markets/{ticker}/history, which does not exist on Kalshi's API -- confirmed empirically on 2026-07-25: every ticker tried, including active high-volume markets, returns a plain-text '404 page not found', never JSON. The function's `if status_code == 404: return []` has silently swallowed this for every call site since it was written, so main.py:364's price-trend/drift-history text in the live report has never actually produced data. Replace the call with the real endpoint, already implemented and tested as core.kalshi.fetch_market_candlesticks() (/series/{series_ticker}/markets/{ticker}/candlesticks) -- this requires threading series_ticker into main.py's per-market loop, which currently only has the raw market dict (series_ticker lives on the event object, not the market object -- confirmed pattern throughout this codebase).
items.notes: Discovered as a side effect of investigating replay-asof-reconstruction's Kalshi-history fallback tier, and deliberately NOT fixed as a drive-by inside that item -- different blast radius (this touches the live pipeline's active call site and a currently-running production feature, not a new backtesting module). fetch_market_candlesticks() itself is done and covered by tests/test_kalshi_settled_fetch.py. SHIPPED 2026-07-25: main.py's step-5 loop (was line 364) now calls fetch_market_candlesticks() using series_ticker already merged onto each market dict at fetch time (main.py line ~155, an existing mechanism -- no new threading needed, the item's own action text overstated this part of the work). period_interval is chosen per horizon: 60 (hourly) for INTRADAY's 1-day lookback so there are enough points to show a trend, 1440 (daily) for every longer horizon. Candlestick price.close_dollars is already on the same 0-1 probability scale the old (dead) code assumed for yes_price, so the existing `start*100`/`end*100` trend-percentage formatting needed no rescaling. Verified against a real ticker (KXCITRINI-28JUL01, MONTHLY horizon): 7 daily candles, '-5.0% (24.0% -> 19.0%) -- declining (7d)' -- correct output where the old code silently produced nothing. fetch_market_history() itself deleted outright (zero remaining callers, zero dedicated tests, so no reason to keep it as a landmine) rather than left as dead code. Full suite still green after the edit. See docs/PROGRESS.md 2026-07-25.

items.title: Kalshi SDK Migration Implementation
items.action: Built the adapter, but not the field-by-field typed-model remapping the Ready-item scope note called for. core/kalshi.py's 16 HTTP-calling functions now route through kalshi-sdk (TexasCoding v9.0.0, pinned in requirements.txt) via a `_sdk_json(config, path, params=)` helper that calls `KalshiClient._transport.request("GET", path, params=params).json()` directly -- deliberately bypassing the SDK's typed resource methods (`client.markets.list()` etc.) entirely, not converting their Pydantic output back to dicts. `_transport` is a private SDK attribute, not a documented public API (confirmed: `KalshiClient` exposes no raw-JSON escape hatch -- checked `dir()` on a live instance), which is exactly why the version is pinned rather than left floating. Reasoning for the deviation: the evaluation's own scope note warned the typed models rename and retype fields (`no_ask_dollars` string -> `no_ask` Decimal) across ~10 response shapes, each needing independent live verification -- real, non-mechanical work. Going under the resource layer instead means every response is the literal JSON `KalshiClient` received off the wire, byte-identical to what the old `requests.get(...).json()` returned, with zero remapping surface and zero per-field verification burden -- a strictly stronger correctness guarantee than hand-verified remapping would have produced, for less work. Every function's public signature, docstring, and business logic (KXMVE-flood day-chunking, near-dated per-day window chunking, the 404-as-empty-list special case on candlesticks, the 401-as-RuntimeError special case on authenticate) is unchanged; only the HTTP call sites changed. `_get_client()` caches one authenticated `KalshiClient` per environment (demo/prod) instead of re-parsing the RSA private key on every single request the way the old code did -- a real efficiency win, verified not to break test isolation (no test exercises the missing-credentials error path, so caching a client across test functions within a run is inert). `fetch_market_candlesticks`'s 404 path now catches `KalshiNotFoundError` (the transport raises rather than returning an inspectable response); `authenticate`'s auth-failure path catches `KalshiAuthError`, which also covers 403 now, not just 401 -- a minor, deliberate improvement, not silently introduced. Updated 31 mock call sites across 3 test files (`test_kalshi_near_dated.py`, `test_kalshi_trades_orderbook.py`, `test_kalshi_settled_fetch.py`) from patching `core.kalshi.requests.get` (a `requests.Response`-shaped mock) to patching `core.kalshi._sdk_json` (returns the raw dict directly, since there's no longer a response object to unwrap) -- mechanical, but real: every `args[0]` URL assertion became `args[1]` (path, no longer prefixed with the full base URL since `_sdk_json` takes a relative path and the SDK's transport does the join), and the one 404 test now mocks a raised `KalshiNotFoundError` instead of a `status_code=404` mock object. Live dry-run (BACKLOG.md's own requirement before touching call sites): wrote a throwaway script that independently reconstructs the pre-migration `requests`-based implementation from this session's earlier full read of the old file (not derived from the new code, so the two paths are genuinely independent) and ran both against the real Kalshi prod API with real credentials for all 16 HTTP-calling functions -- authenticate, fetch_markets, fetch_market, fetch_trades, fetch_recent_trades, fetch_events, fetch_event_markets, fetch_event_detail, fetch_near_dated_markets, fetch_settled_events, fetch_settled_event_markets, fetch_market_candlesticks (both the 200 and 404 paths), fetch_market_with_retry, fetch_orderbook, fetch_fills, fetch_positions. 15/16 exact-matched; the one difference (`/portfolio/balance`'s `updated_ts`, off by 1-2 seconds between runs) is the wall-clock gap between the two sequential live calls to a field that reflects live server time, not a code discrepancy -- reproduced twice, always equal to the measured gap between calls. All read-only GETs; no orders, no state mutation, no real-money risk. Full suite: 2117 passed, 1 skipped, 13 subtests passed, 0 failed.

items.title: Kalshi Sdk Evaluation 2026 08
items.action: Live-tested both SDK candidates against the real Kalshi API with real credentials (read-only calls: get_balance, get_markets), not just docs/README research. Official `kalshi_python_sync` (Kalshi/exchange-infra v3.26.0): full REST coverage matching all 21 of core/kalshi.py's functions (MarketApi/EventsApi/HistoricalApi/PortfolioApi cover markets/events/candlesticks/orderbook/trades/fills/positions). Found a real bug while live-testing: `ApiClient.set_kalshi_auth()` raises `NameError` -- `KalshiAuth` is never imported in api_client.py, so the documented auth-setup convenience method is broken in the currently published version (worked around by importing `KalshiAuth` directly and setting `client.kalshi_auth` manually). Also uses `salt_length=PSS.DIGEST_LENGTH` for its RSA-PSS signing vs core/kalshi.py's `MAX_LENGTH` -- confirmed live against Kalshi's real server that both salt lengths are accepted (server-side verification is permissive), so this isn't a compatibility blocker, just a documented difference. Community candidate's real PyPI package name is `kalshi-sdk` (not `kalshi-python-sdk` as originally assumed from the GitHub repo name) by TexasCoding, v9.0.0: broader scope confirmed (REST+WebSocket+FIX+Perps, resource-style API like `client.portfolio.balance()`/`client.markets.list()`), auth worked cleanly with no bugs found, returns `Decimal`-typed prices and `datetime`-typed timestamps with `_all`-suffixed auto-pagination helpers and `.to_dataframe()` export -- only 4 GitHub stars, still a real trust-footprint gap vs the official package despite cleaner code in this test. Both SDKs return fully-typed model objects (Pydantic), not the raw dicts with string timestamps/prices core/kalshi.py currently returns and every consumer (main.py, analysis/*, scripts/*, and their tests) currently expects -- confirms the backlog's original caution that this is a genuine typed-model migration, not a drop-in dependency swap. Recommendation: an adapter layer inside core/kalshi.py (converts SDK responses back to the existing dict contract) rather than propagating typed models through the whole codebase -- see kalshi-sdk-migration-implementation (Done, below) for the scoped follow-up -- landed via the transport layer directly rather than the typed resource methods, sidestepping the field-by-field remapping this note anticipated.
items.notes: Added retroactively to reconcile backlog.json with BACKLOG.md, which had been hand-edited directly for several recent Done items without a matching backlog.json update.

items.title: Whale Flag Lv Guarantee
items.action: User asked why the run header's whale-flag count (e.g. "15 whale flags") never seemed to show up as detail in the report. Traced it: core.report.compute_leviathan_score() only awarded any whale-related bonus when BOTH whale_detected AND ob_flag fired together (+3) -- a whale-only flag got zero LV bonus. With BASE=40 and core.scorer.score_markets()'s pre-Claude gate at config.scoring.min_pre_claude_lv=20 (confirmed live in config.json), a whale-flagged market with otherwise weak/negative signals (net_edge<=0, pass_count>=3, short horizon -- realistic combination, stacks to -21) could score as low as 19-23, sometimes below the gate. A market that fails the gate never reaches Claude scoring at all: no cs result comes back, so main.py's `if not cs: continue` skips it before it can become a final_signal, a logged PASS, OR a whale_only report row -- it vanishes from the report entirely, with the only trace being the raw pre-gate count printed in step 5, before scoring ever runs. Confirmed materially real on the pipeline run earlier this session: 18 markets flagged, only 6 reached Claude (min_pre_claude_lv=20 was the binding filter, well under max_markets_per_run=10), so some of that run's 15 whale flags plausibly never got a Claude estimate or any report visibility at all. Fix: whale_detected alone now adds +4 (BASE 40 + 4 = 44, the same safety margin watchlist_signal's existing +4 bonus already has), replacing the old both-required +3 -- not an addition on top of it, per explicit user sign-off on the exact diff via AskUserQuestion (two other options -- a pre-filtered-whale-flags visibility section, or both -- were offered and declined). ob_flag alone still contributes nothing on its own; only whale_detected changed. 4 new tests (compute_leviathan_score: whale-alone +4, whale_detected=False no bonus, whale-without-ob-flag still gets the bonus (regression guard against reintroducing the combined-only gate); score_markets integration: a market at LV 19 that fails the gate on its own now clears it at LV 23 once whale_detected is added, reaching the CLI batch step). Full suite: 2122 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed.

items.title: Whale Only None Direction Crash
items.action: Real production incident, same day as whale-flag-lv-guarantee shipped: a manually-triggered 2026-08-05 run (real Kalshi/Claude calls, same as any scheduled run) crashed inside compile_report() with `TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()` and sent no report at all (caught by main.py's step-8 except block, fell through to the unsent-report fallback, no email went out). Root cause: core.whales sets whale_direction=None (not absent from the dict) whenever whale_detected fires purely from volume-spike/block-trade activity with no clear directional lean -- independent of whale_detected itself. The WHALE ACTIVITY table's row-builder used `w.get("whale_direction", "?")`, and dict.get(key, default) only substitutes the default for a MISSING key, not a present key whose value is None -- so None flowed into _render_table's _cell(), which unconditionally does `len(val)`. This exact shape had apparently never reached this render path before; whale-flag-lv-guarantee (shipped the same session) made a whale-only, no-clear-direction flag reaching this table far more likely by guaranteeing whale_detected clears the pre-Claude min_pre_claude_lv gate instead of silently dropping out beforehand -- the fix that closed one visibility gap opened this crash on the very next scheduled run. Fixed by switching to `w.get(key) or default` (the same None-safe pattern already used for this identical field in _week_whale_rows, just not in this table) for all three string fields in the row (ticker, whale_direction, title) -- ratio was already crash-safe (falsy-checked before formatting). 2 new tests (None whale_direction, None ticker/title), full suite green. Did not re-run the pipeline to recover the missed 2026-08-05 report as part of this fix -- that is a real-money-adjacent action (another live Kalshi/Claude run + a real email) left for explicit go-ahead, not bundled into a bug fix.

items.title: Resolved Count Metric Desync
items.action: backlog/checker.py::compute_metrics()'s resolved_count SQL diverged from core/logger.py::get_stats()['resolved'] (the number scripts/gate_notifier.py's actual gate-unlock emails use) two ways: no direction filter (counted PASS-direction rows, which resolve LOSS by construction -- see export-validation-pass-exclusion) and no source filter (counted real_fill/research_probe rows, tracked as separate populations from paper signals by design). Live data went 47 (buggy) -> 16 (direction fix alone) -> 13 (both fixes, exact match with get_stats()['resolved']). Caught by manually cross-checking BACKLOG.md's own regeneration metrics against gate_notifier's gate_state.json during a housekeeping pass after a 10-day gap; the source-filter half of the bug wasn't visible until the direction fix alone still left a 16-vs-13 gap, traced by breaking the resolved non-PASS rows down by source (paper=13, real_fill=2, research_probe=1). Practical effect before the fix: checker.py/BACKLOG.md's header and Locked/Ready gates could read edge-decay-analysis (resolved_count>=30) or calibration-curve (>=50) as closer to unlocking, or unlocked outright, than the codebase's own established "resolved" definition actually supports -- gate_notifier.py's separate, correct implementation meant no bad unlock *email* was ever sent, but BACKLOG.md itself would have misrepresented state to anyone reading the file directly. resolved_count_per_category_max was deliberately left untouched: its two implementations already agreed (neither excludes PASS), and unlike headline resolved_count there's a real argument PASS rows belong in a per-heuristic calibration scorecard, not just paper-trading P&L. Fix applied to both SQL filters (`AND direction != 'PASS' AND (source = 'paper' OR source IS NULL)`). Test fixture (tmp_db in tests/test_backlog_checker.py) gained a direction column plus PASS/real_fill/research_probe resolved rows to cover the exclusion directly; 1 new test, full suite green (2125 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed).

items.title: Whale Actionability Scorecard
items.action: User asked what we're actually doing with whale-flag data beyond identifying it -- the report's WHALE ACTIVITY table just lists sightings (a market a whale traded, no track record attached), so there was no way to tell if following whale activity has predicted anything. Same gap as per-heuristic-scorecard: core/logger.py::get_stats_by_whale() (win rate/P&L/avg_edge for whale-flagged vs not, resolved YES/NO paper signals only) already existed and was already displayed in analysis/calibration.py, but never reached the actual email report. Added a "Win Rate: Whale-Flagged vs Not" section (Group/Total/Wins/Win%/P&L/AvgEdge, two rows, groups with zero resolved total omitted rather than printed as a bogus 0-row) to compile_report (daily text) and both weekly digest renderers, mirroring per-heuristic-scorecard's exact footprint and precedent (NOT added to render_html, the daily HTML, for the same reason). Also added a verdict line (win-rate delta between the two groups, "whale flag predicts wins" / "underperforms" / "no meaningful difference yet") -- same pattern as the existing LV-grade A-vs-D verdict line already in both renderers. Wired into main.py's three call sites (including the unsent-report fallback path, for consistency with every other stats param there). 9 new tests, full suite: 2144 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. Live-verified against the real DB: n=1 whale-flagged resolved signal right now (100% win rate, +$0.49) vs n=12 non-whale (33%, -$0.42) -- textbook too-small-to-mean-anything, but the section renders correctly and the plumbing is ready the moment more data exists.
